paper_core_claims.claim: Operator learning is supervised approximation of a map between separable Banach function spaces using finite input-output function samples, explicit empirical/population risk, and held-out or shifted test measures.

PCA-Net and DeepONet expose finite latent encoders/decoders, FNO lifts neural-network layers to function space through integral/Fourier operators, and random features trade full parameter training for a convex coefficient problem.

Universal approximation establishes existence for broad operator classes with unrestricted model size, data, and optimization; the review explicitly calls it necessary but insufficient for feasible learning.
paper_core_claims.anchors: Section 4 opening; Theorems 4.1-4.5; Corollary 4.6; Section 6; PDF pages 11-16 and 30

paper_core_claims.claim: Quantitative complexity depends sharply on the operator class: linear and holomorphic structure can yield useful rates, whereas general Lipschitz or Frechet-differentiable operators face exponential parameter and sample lower bounds under standard architectures.
Efficient approximation results for specific PDE operators often rely on explicit formulae or emulation of numerical algorithms, but a general characterization of exploitable structure is still open.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A function is an element of a Banach function space over a spatial or spatiotemporal domain. The target object is an operator between such spaces, approximated by a finite-parameter learned map and evaluated relative to a probability measure, norm, risk, accuracy, and structural class.

representation_or_carrier.problem_carrier: Banach input/output spaces, target operator, input measure, and sampled function pairs
representation_or_carrier.latent_carrier: PCA coefficients, sensor values, learned branch/trunk bases, and encoder-decoder coordinates
representation_or_carrier.function_space_carrier: integral kernels, Fourier coefficients, channel-valued hidden functions, and averaging neural-operator states
representation_or_carrier.artifact_carrier: finite parameters for PCA-Net, DeepONet, FNO, or random-feature coefficients and fixed random operators
representation_or_carrier.analysis_carrier: norm/risk, compact set, model size, sample count, smoothness or holomorphy, bit complexity, n-width, and accuracy epsilon

specification_language: The specification is mathematical and statistical: spaces U/V, target operator, domain constraints, input distribution, error or relative-error metric, empirical and population risks, architecture family, and accuracy/complexity target. PDE examples add coefficient bounds and boundary conditions. There is no general-purpose FunctionSpec DSL, effect declaration, permission, or deployment contract.

compiler_or_generator.encoder_decoder_path: encode functions to finite coordinates, learn a finite-dimensional mapping, and reconstruct an output function
compiler_or_generator.function_space_path: compose learned pointwise maps with nonlocal integral or Fourier layers without a conceptual finite latent bottleneck
compiler_or_generator.random_feature_path: sample fixed operator features and solve a convex coefficient optimization
compiler_or_generator.training: choose parameters by empirical risk or architecture-specific approximation procedures
compiler_or_generator.boundary: These are learning and approximation pipelines, not semantics-preserving compilation from a symbolic contract.

interpreter_or_runtime: Runtime depends on the artifact: PCA projection and reconstruction, DeepONet branch/trunk evaluation, FFT-based truncated Fourier layers, or a sum of fixed random operator features. Practical realization discretizes functions and applies numerical kernels or transforms; the review supplies no single universal runtime or safety contract.
composition_rule: Encoder-decoder artifacts compose as G_V after a finite map after F_U. FNO/ANO artifacts compose input lifting, repeated integral-affine-nonlinear layers, and output projection. These are typed mathematical compositions, but the review does not define arbitrary artifact linking, runtime routing, fallback, or conflict resolution.
state_or_effect_model: Hidden functions, latent vectors, Fourier modes, and learned coefficients carry numerical state through evaluation. PDE boundary and positivity constraints affect problem validity. No general software effects, mutation, I/O, exceptions, permissions, transactions, rollback, or persistent trace schema is defined.
uncertainty_model: The review explicitly treats probability measures over input functions, empirical versus population risk, noisy linear-operator data, Gaussian priors and posteriors, expected approximation error, sample complexity, and out-of-distribution test measures. These are problem-specific statistical semantics, not a unified calibrated per-call uncertainty or fuzzy execution model.

validation_regime.qualitative: universal-approximation existence on compact sets or in Bochner norms under space and continuity assumptions
validation_regime.quantitative: parameter, bit, sample, encoding, reconstruction, and neural-network approximation bounds for defined operator classes
validation_regime.negative: n-width and architecture-specific lower bounds exposing parametric and sample complexity
validation_regime.empirical_context: the review summarizes published applications but does not itself provide a new common empirical benchmark
validation_regime.boundary: theoretical understanding is explicitly incomplete and many efficient results remain operator-specific

equivalence_notions.boundary: An artifact approximates the target under a specified norm, input measure, and test distribution; this is not exact semantic identity.
Input encoding, finite mapping, and output reconstruction each contribute error, so the latent representation is not inherently equivalent to the original function.
Arbitrary accuracy can require unconstrained parameters, data, and optimization and therefore does not imply feasible or learned equivalence.
Algebraic rates rely on holomorphy, Barron/RKHS membership, explicit formulae, or emulable numerical algorithms; general smoothness is insufficient.
No semantics is provided for effectful programs, external state, or arbitrary computational functions.

lifecycle_and_provenance: The review identifies architecture definitions, source literature, training/testing measures, mathematical assumptions, error decompositions, and publication version. It does not define stable learned-artifact IDs, data/model signatures, environment capture, registry promotion, drift monitoring, supersession, rollback, or retirement.
limitations_and_failure_boundaries: Universal approximation is qualitative and does not guarantee feasible model size, data volume, or optimizer success.
Encoder-decoder methods incur separately compounding input-encoding, finite-map, and output-reconstruction errors.
FNO is conceptually function-space based but practical FFT implementations impose grids and Fourier truncation.
General Lipschitz or Frechet-differentiable operator classes can require exponentially many parameters, bits, or samples with standard architectures.
Nonstandard activations can reduce parameter counts while moving complexity into bit precision or architecture description.
Holomorphic, Barron, RKHS, or numerical-emulation rates depend on restrictive or currently hard-to-verify structure.
Efficient theory for many PDE operators is case-by-case, and the general exploitable structure remains an open problem.
The review does not establish optimizer convergence for the fully trained architectures used in practice.
The mathematical operator setting does not supply effects, safety, persistent traces, runtime routing, or lifecycle governance.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: It does not claim that universal approximation makes a trained artifact equivalent to its target or practically efficient.
It does not show that all neural operators beat the curse of dimensionality or parametric complexity.
It does not provide one architecture-independent compiler, interpreter, trace, router, or registry.
It does not validate the point architecture as a whole or turn a literature review into proof or production evidence.

corrections: The provisional card incorrectly lists the authors as Boullé et al.; the paper is by Nikola B. Kovachki, Samuel Lanthaler, and Andrew M. Stuart.
The provisional section list is inaccurate: the paper has six main sections and devotes its largest analytical section to quantitative error and complexity, including negative lower bounds.
The review does address general Lipschitz operators, statistical risks, noisy data, sample complexity, and equivalence boundaries, not only PDE-specific universal approximation.
The full review supports a bounded CONFIRMED projection across Representation, Artifact, and Validator, while general software effects and lifecycle remain unsupported.

confirmed_projection: The review directly supports a bounded FunctionSpec-Representation-Artifact-Validator projection by distinguishing operator specifications, carrier families, training/testing risks, qualitative universality, quantitative complexity, and lower-bound failure regimes across major operator-learning architectures.
source_specific_reasoning: This review is especially valuable because it prevents four common category errors: functions are not merely large vectors; a latent encoding is not lossless by default; universal approximation is not feasible learned equivalence; and empirical success does not erase exponential lower bounds for broad operator classes. It also compares multiple artifact and runtime carriers and explains when problem structure, rather than generic smoothness, supports efficient approximation. The CONFIRMED status is therefore strong but narrow: it covers an operator-learning architecture and validation projection, not arbitrary computational functions, effectful semantics, runtime routing, trace persistence, or lifecycle governance.
projection_boundary: All GAP and Function OS impacts above are 121CX architectural projections from the review's bounded synthesis of cited results. Mathematical theorems retain their cited assumptions, and this model review is not itself proof, causal identification, empirical validation of the point architecture, or final truth freeze.
